name: Iran nuclear programme
value: No IAEA access; US-Israel weigh new strikes
summary: US and Israel are weighing a new assault on Iran, CBS reports; Iran calls keeping its enriched uranium a red line
state: CBS News reported on 20 Nov that Israel and the US are considering a new military assault on Iran, with Israel concerned about missile rebuilding and sites moving underground; monitors believe Iran still holds about 900 pounds of uranium enriched to 60%. Foreign Minister Araghchi said on 21 Nov that keeping highly enriched uranium in Iran is a red line (The New Arab). Iran rejected IAEA Board resolutions on 14 Nov and normal inspections have not resumed. No strike on a nuclear site or NPT withdrawal was found, so Watch holds.
for_you: A renewed strike campaign would raise risks for people and shipping across the Gulf. Anyone in or travelling to the region can follow FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Watch: 60% stockpile with inspector access curtailed, plus credible strike threats (CBS, 20 Nov)

sources.title: CBS News — U.S. and Israel considering new assault on Iran, sources say
The New Arab — Qatari delegation visits Iran for talks to end war with US

why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.
drivers: Enrichment levels, IAEA access, Israeli/US military posture, snapback sanctions, talks.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
